chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dhurayḥ ibn Muḥammad al-Muḥāribī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who forgets to pronounce the takbīr until he has recited. He said: He should pronounce the takbīr.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man; the person being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.قَرَأَ: he recited; began the recitation in the prayer
key_terms.يَنْسَىٰ: forgets; fails to perform an act due to forgetfulness
key_terms.يُكَبِّرَ: to pronounce the takbīr; to say 'Allāhu Akbar'

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ until after beginning recitation in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets the opening takbīr of salat (prayer) until after beginning recitation. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that he should still pronounce the takbīr, indicating the practical correction for this lapse within the prayer.
